A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed focal segmental necrotizing lesions and cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
She received cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoids for remission induction. At her current assessment, her constitutional and skin manifestations have resolved. Her blood pressure is 132/80 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Serum creatinine has improved to 1.3 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 51 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein, with 2 to 4 red blood cells per high-power field and no red blood cell casts. Proteinuria has decreased to 0.2 g/day. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0.
The treating team is choosing between azathioprine and mycophenolate mofetil for maintenance therapy, and the treating physician is wondering which would be the better option. Which of the following best reflects the available evidence?
A. Azathioprine is favored because it prevents relapse more effectively than mycophenolate mofetil but causes substantially more infections
B. Mycophenolate mofetil is favored because it prevents relapse more effectively than azathioprine while producing fewer infections
C. Mycophenolate mofetil is favored because it provides similar relapse prevention to azathioprine with a superior infection profile
D. Azathioprine is favored because mycophenolate mofetil is less effective at preventing relapse and does not provide a superior infection profile
E. Either agent is equally appropriate because relapse prevention and infection outcomes are equivalent with both maintenance strategies
PART B - Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. Azathioprine is favored because mycophenolate mofetil is less effective at preventing relapse and does not provide a superior infection profile
PART C - Explanation
This patient has achieved remission following induction therapy for ANCA-associated vasculitis. Her systemic manifestations have resolved, kidney function has substantially improved, urinary abnormalities have markedly decreased, and her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0. The clinical decision therefore concerns selection of maintenance therapy to prevent subsequent relapse.
According to KDIGO, mycophenolate mofetil was less effective than azathioprine for prevention of relapse when the two agents were compared as maintenance therapy. Importantly, mycophenolate mofetil did not provide a superior infection profile. Therefore, a potential assumption that mycophenolate mofetil might trade similar relapse prevention for fewer infections is not supported by the available evidence.

title: Q068 · The treating physician is considering whether the negative ANCA result after 12 months of maintenance means that prolonged azathioprine therapy is unlikely to provide additional benefit. Which of the following best reflects the available evidence?
body: A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with proteinase 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis 18 months ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and rapidly declini
full:
A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with proteinase 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis 18 months ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and rapidly declining kidney function. At diagnosis, her serum creatinine had increased from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.8 mg/dL over 5 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 79 to 20 mL/min/1.73 m2. Proteinase 3 ANCA testing was positive and myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was negative.
Urinalysis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimated proteinuria of 1.7 g/day.
A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed focal segmental necrotizing lesions and cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
She achieved remission following cyclophosphamide-based induction and subsequently received azathioprine maintenance therapy. She has now completed 12 months of azathioprine treatment. Her blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Serum creatinine is stable at 1.3 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 51 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein, with 2 to 4 red blood cells per high-power field and no red blood cell casts. Proteinuria is 0.2 g/day, her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0, and proteinase 3 ANCA testing has become negative.
The treating physician is considering whether the negative ANCA result after 12 months of maintenance means that prolonged azathioprine therapy is unlikely to provide additional benefit. Which of the following best reflects the available evidence?
A. ANCA negativity alone does not establish that prolonged azathioprine lacks benefit, because the benefit of longer therapy did not differ according to ANCA serotype or ANCA status after 12 months
B. ANCA negativity after 12 months identifies patients who no longer benefit from prolonged azathioprine and should routinely have maintenance therapy withdrawn
C. Prolonged azathioprine benefits only patients who remain ANCA-positive after 12 months, regardless of whether their original disease was PR3-ANCA or MPO-ANCA associated
D. Prolonged azathioprine benefits patients with MPO-ANCA disease but not those with PR3-ANCA disease once clinical remission and ANCA negativity are achieved
E. ANCA status after 12 months completely determines the appropriate duration of azathioprine maintenance regardless of the patient’s clinical relapse risk
PART B - Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. ANCA negativity alone does not establish that prolonged azathioprine lacks benefit, because the benefit of longer therapy did not differ according to ANCA serotype or ANCA status after 12 months
PART C - Explanation
This patient has achieved sustained clinical remission while receiving azathioprine maintenance therapy. Her systemic manifestations have resolved, kidney function is stable, urinary abnormalities have markedly improved, Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0, and proteinase 3 ANCA has become negative. The question concerns whether this serologic conversion should be used to conclude that longer azathioprine maintenance has no additional value.
According to KDIGO, studies comparing earlier tapering of azathioprine after 12 months with prolonged treatment found that longer azathioprine maintenance reduced relapse and kidney failure. Importantly, the benefits of longer-duration therapy did not differ between patients with proteinase 3 ANCA and myeloperoxidase ANCA, or between patients who remained ANCA-positive and those who became ANCA-negative after 12 months.

PART C - Explanation

The question therefore concerns how maintenance rituximab should be scheduled rather than whether active disease requires treatment.
According to KDIGO, rituximab maintenance can be administered on a fixed schedule or using a tailored approach based on reappearance of CD19-positive B cells and/or ANCA. In MAINRITSAN2, these two strategies prevented relapse similarly. However, the tailored approach required fewer rituximab infusions. No difference in adverse events was reported.

title: Q070 · The treating physician is deciding whether long-term maintenance immunosuppression should be started. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach in this patient?
body: A 64-year-old man was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis 8 months ago after presenting with fatigue, reduced urine output, and rapidly progressive kidney failure. He had no hist
full:
A 64-year-old man was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis 8 months ago after presenting with fatigue, reduced urine output, and rapidly progressive kidney failure. He had no history of pulmonary, upper respiratory, neurologic, ocular, or skin manifestations. At diagnosis, his serum creatinine had increased from 1.1 mg/dL to 7.6 mg/dL over 4 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 72 to 7 mL/min/1.73 m2. Myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was positive and proteinase 3 ANCA testing was negative.
Urinalysis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 40 to 50 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimated proteinuria of 2.1 g/day. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis. Hemodialysis was initiated, and he received induction immunosuppressive therapy.
At his current assessment, he remains dialysis-dependent but has no constitutional symptoms or other manifestations of active vasculitis. His blood pressure is 134/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. A thorough review for extrarenal disease, including chest computed tomography, shows no pulmonary or other extrarenal involvement. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0.
The treating physician is deciding whether long-term maintenance immunosuppression should be started. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach in this patient?
A. Rituximab maintenance should be given routinely because dialysis dependence substantially increases the risk of extrarenal relapse
B. Maintenance therapy may not be necessary because relapse risk is low and the risks of long-term immunosuppression may outweigh the benefits
C. Azathioprine maintenance should be given routinely because persistent kidney failure indicates ongoing active ANCA-associated vasculitis
D. Maintenance therapy should be continued indefinitely because myeloperoxidase ANCA positivity predicts frequent relapse despite the absence of extrarenal disease
E. Maintenance therapy should be intensified because dialysis dependence after induction indicates treatment-resistant systemic vasculitis
PART B - Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. Maintenance therapy may not be necessary because relapse risk is low and the risks of long-term immunosuppression may outweigh the benefits
PART C - Explanation
This patient has myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis that presented predominantly with kidney failure. He remains dialysis-dependent after induction therapy but has achieved complete clinical control of vasculitis, with a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 and no pulmonary, neurologic, skin, upper respiratory, ocular, or other extrarenal manifestations. A thorough evaluation, including chest computed tomography, has not identified occult extrarenal disease.
According to KDIGO, patients with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis who are dialysis-dependent and have no extrarenal manifestations represent a subgroup with a relatively low risk of relapse. In this setting, the risks of long-term maintenance immunosuppression, particularly infectious complications, may outweigh the benefits of relapse prevention. The need for maintenance therapy should therefore be assessed individually, and long-term maintenance may not be necessary.

A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed focal segmental necrotizing lesions and cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.

Serum creatinine is stable at 1.3 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 66 mL/min/1.73 m2. The treating physician is reviewing how long maintenance therapy should generally be continued before withdrawal is considered. Which of the following best reflects the recommended duration?
A. Between 3 and 6 months after induction of remission, regardless of relapse risk or the maintenance drug used
B. Between 18 months and 4 years after induction of remission, individualized according to relapse risk and the maintenance drug used
C. Exactly 12 months after induction of remission, with treatment stopped once clinical remission has been sustained
D. At least 5 years after induction of remission in all patients, regardless of serotype, relapse history, or treatment choice

This patient has achieved sustained remission after induction therapy and remains clinically stable on maintenance treatment. The question therefore concerns the appropriate duration of maintenance therapy rather than management of active disease.
According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.3.2.2, the optimal duration of maintenance therapy is between 18 months and 4 years after induction of remission. The duration should be individualized according to factors such as the patient’s risk of relapse and the maintenance drug being used.

title: Q072 · The treating physician is considering an alternative maintenance agent following azathioprine intolerance. Which of the following best reflects the role of methotrexate in this patient?
body: A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis 14 months ago after presenting with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At dia
full:

Myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was positive and proteinase 3 ANCA testing was negative.

A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed focal segmental necrotizing lesions and cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
She achieved remission following induction therapy and subsequently began azathioprine maintenance. Azathioprine was later discontinued because she could not tolerate the medication. At her current assessment, she remains in clinical remission. Her blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 68 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein, with 2 to 4 red blood cells per high-power field and no red blood cell casts. The treating physician is considering an alternative maintenance agent following azathioprine intolerance. Which of the following best reflects the role of methotrexate in this patient?
A. Methotrexate should be reserved for patients with a GFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 because reduced kidney function favors its use
B. Methotrexate should be avoided because any previous ANCA-associated kidney involvement precludes its use for maintenance
C. Methotrexate may be considered as an alternative maintenance agent because her GFR is above 60 mL/min/1.73 m2

Her kidney function has substantially recovered, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 68 mL/min/1.73 m2, and she has no evidence of current active vasculitis.
According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.3.2.4, methotrexate or mycophenolate mofetil may be considered as alternatives to azathioprine for maintenance therapy in patients who are intolerant of azathioprine. However, methotrexate should not be used when GFR is below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2.

title: Q074 · The treating physician is considering whether maintenance immunosuppression can now be withdrawn. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach?

full:
A 42-year-old man with PR 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis was originally diagnosed 3 years ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, recurrent otitis media, progressive hearing loss, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At diagnosis, his serum creatinine had increased from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.7 mg/dL over 5 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 109 to 29 mL/min/1.73 m2. Kidney biopsy demonstrated focal segmental necrosis and cellular crescents involving 9 of 20 glomeruli, with minimal immunoglobulin and complement staining on immunofluorescence.
He achieved remission after induction therapy but experienced a subsequent relapse characterized by recurrent nasal symptoms, worsening ear symptoms with further hearing impairment, purpura, and renewed glomerular hematuria. During this relapse, his serum creatinine increased from 1.3 to 2.1 mg/dL over 3 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 70 to 39 mL/min/1.73 m2. He underwent another course of induction therapy and again achieved clinical remission. Proteinase 3 ANCA remained positive at the end of induction at 48 U/mL.

His blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Serum creatinine is stable at 1.3 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 70 mL/min/1.73 m2. The treating physician is considering whether maintenance immunosuppression can now be withdrawn. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach?
A. Withdraw maintenance therapy because persistent ANCA positivity at the end of induction does not contribute to assessment of future relapse risk
B. Stop maintenance therapy because completion of 18 months of treatment outweighs previous relapse and ear, nose, and throat disease when remission is present
C. Stop maintenance therapy because stable kidney function and a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 eliminate the prognostic importance of prior relapse
D. Exercise caution with withdrawal because his PR3-ANCA disease, prior relapse, ear and upper respiratory involvement, and persistent ANCA positivity indicate a higher relapse-risk profile
E. Continue maintenance therapy indefinitely because the presence of any single relapse-risk factor precludes future withdrawal of immunosuppression
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. Exercise caution with withdrawal because his PR3-ANCA disease, prior relapse, ear and upper respiratory involvement, and persistent ANCA positivity indicate a higher relapse-risk profile
PART C — Explanation
This patient is currently in clinical remission, but the decision to withdraw maintenance therapy should not be based solely on the duration of treatment or the absence of current disease manifestations. According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.3.2.3, relapse risk should be considered when maintenance therapy is being withdrawn.
KDIGO identifies several factors associated with increased relapse risk. Relevant factors in this patient include proteinase 3 ANCA-associated disease, a history of previous relapse, ear, nose, and throat disease, and ANCA positivity at the end of induction. His recurrent otitis media, nasal disease, and hearing impairment therefore contribute clinically relevant information when assessing whether maintenance treatment should now be withdrawn.

title: Q076 · The treating physician is considering either another cyclophosphamide course or rituximab for reinduction. Which of the following best incorporates the significance of this patient’s previous treatment exposure?
body: A 49-year-old man with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis was initially diagnosed 6 years ago after presenting with fatigue, purpura, dark-colored urine, and rapidly declining kidney function.
full:
A 49-year-old man with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis was initially diagnosed 6 years ago after presenting with fatigue, purpura, dark-colored urine, and rapidly declining kidney function. Myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was positive and proteinase 3 ANCA testing was negative. He subsequently achieved remission, and during his most recent stable period his serum creatinine was 1.3 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 59 mL/min/1.73 m2.
He now presents with a 2-week history of recurrent fatigue, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 150/86 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and temperature is 37.0 C. Serum creatinine has increased to 2.5 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate has decreased to 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimates proteinuria of 1.5 g/day. The findings are consistent with another clinically significant relapse requiring induction therapy.
The treating physician is considering either another cyclophosphamide course or rituximab for reinduction. Which of the following best incorporates the significance of this patient’s previous treatment exposure?
A. Favor cyclophosphamide because previous cumulative exposure does not influence treatment selection during subsequent relapses
B. Favor cyclophosphamide because cumulative exposure above 36 g predicts greater remission efficacy with additional cyclophosphamide treatment
C. Favor rituximab because cumulative cyclophosphamide exposure above 36 g has been associated with malignancy and should be considered before giving further cyclophosphamide
D. Favor rituximab only after cumulative cyclophosphamide exposure exceeds 50 g because lower cumulative doses have no recognized long-term concern
E. Use either agent without considering cumulative cyclophosphamide exposure because malignancy risk is unrelated to total treatment received
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. Favor rituximab because cumulative cyclophosphamide exposure above 36 g has been associated with malignancy and should be considered before giving further cyclophosphamide
PART C — Explanation
This patient has relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis and has already received substantial cyclophosphamide exposure during previous treatment courses. His cumulative lifetime cyclophosphamide dose is 38 g.
According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.3.3.1, when considering whether cyclophosphamide should be used again for relapsing disease, the cumulative amount already administered should be taken into account. Cumulative cyclophosphamide doses above 36 g have been associated with the occurrence of malignancies. Rituximab is also preferred for relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis, making avoidance of additional cyclophosphamide particularly attractive when an appropriate alternative is available.

title: Q077 · Rituximab has been selected for maintenance therapy using the MAINRITSAN scheduled dosing protocol. Which of the following regimens most closely matches this maintenance schedule?
body: A 57-year-old woman was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis 6 months ago after presenting with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At diag
full:
A 57-year-old woman was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis 6 months ago after presenting with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At diagnosis, her serum creatinine had increased from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.8 mg/dL over 5 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 75 to 20 mL/min/1.73 m2. Myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was positive and proteinase 3 ANCA testing was negative.
Urinalysis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimated proteinuria of 1.7 g/day.
A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed focal segmental necrotizing lesions and cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
She received cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and has now achieved complete clinical remission. Her blood pressure is 132/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Serum creatinine has improved to 1.3 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 52 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein, with 2 to 4 red blood cells per high-power field and no red blood cell casts. Proteinuria is 0.2 g/day, and her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0.
Rituximab has been selected for maintenance therapy using the MAINRITSAN scheduled dosing protocol. Which of the following regimens most closely matches this maintenance schedule?
A. Rituximab 1000 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by 1000 mg at months 6, 12, and 18
B. Rituximab 500 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by 500 mg every 4 months through month 16
C. Rituximab 500 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by 500 mg at months 6, 12, and 18
D. Rituximab 500 mg as a single dose at complete remission, followed by 500 mg at months 3, 6, 9, and 12
E. Rituximab 1000 mg at complete remission, followed by 1000 mg at months 4, 8, 12, and 16
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. Rituximab 500 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by 500 mg at months 6, 12, and 18
PART C — Explanation
This patient has achieved complete remission following induction therapy and has already been selected for rituximab maintenance. The question therefore focuses specifically on the scheduled rituximab maintenance regimen used in MAINRITSAN.
According to KDIGO,, the MAINRITSAN scheduled dosing protocol consists of rituximab 500 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by rituximab 500 mg at months 6, 12, and 18.

title: Q078 · Rituximab has been selected for maintenance therapy using the RITAZAREM regimen studied in relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis. Which of the following schedules most closely matches this maintenance protocol?
body: A 51-year-old man with proteinase 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis was initially diagnosed 3 years ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and rapidly d
full:
A 51-year-old man with proteinase 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis was initially diagnosed 3 years ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and rapidly declining kidney function. At diagnosis, his serum creatinine had increased from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.8 mg/dL over 5 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 103 to 26 mL/min/1.73 m2. Proteinase 3 ANCA testing was positive and myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was negative.
Urinalysis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimated proteinuria of 1.7 g/day. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis. He received induction therapy and subsequently achieved remission.
Eighteen months later, he developed recurrent nasal symptoms, purpura, and dark-colored urine. Serum creatinine increased from 1.3 mg/dL to 2.5 mg/dL, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 67 to 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis again demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with dysmorphic red blood cells and red blood cell casts. Proteinuria increased from 0.2 g/day to 1.5 g/day. He was diagnosed with relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis and received rituximab for remission reinduction.
At his current assessment, his nasal and skin manifestations have resolved. His blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Serum creatinine has improved to 1.4 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 61 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein, with 2 to 4 red blood cells per high-power field and no red blood cell casts. Proteinuria is 0.2 g/day, and his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0.
Rituximab has been selected for maintenance therapy using the RITAZAREM regimen studied in relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis. Which of the following schedules most closely matches this maintenance protocol?
A. Rituximab 1000 mg after induction of remission, followed by 1000 mg at months 6, 12, and 18 after the first infusion
B. Rituximab 1000 mg after induction of remission, followed by 1000 mg at months 4, 8, 12, and 16 after the first infusion
C. Rituximab 500 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by 500 mg at months 4, 8, 12, and 16
D. Rituximab 1000 mg for 2 doses at complete remission, followed by 500 mg at months 6, 12, and 18
E. Rituximab 500 mg after induction of remission, followed by 500 mg every 2 months through month 16
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. Rituximab 1000 mg after induction of remission, followed by 1000 mg at months 4, 8, 12, and 16 after the first infusion
PART C — Explanation
This patient has relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis that has again entered remission following rituximab reinduction. His systemic manifestations have resolved, kidney function has improved, active glomerular urinary findings have subsided, and his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0. Rituximab has already been selected for maintenance, so the question specifically tests the dosing schedule used in RITAZAREM.
According to KDIGO, the RITAZAREM maintenance regimen consists of a rituximab 1000 mg infusion after induction of remission, followed by additional 1000 mg infusions at months 4, 8, 12, and 16 after the first infusion. RITAZAREM specifically studied patients with relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis.

title: Q079 · The transplant team is considering postponing transplantation solely because ANCA remains detectable. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach?
body: A 46-year-old woman with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis developed kidney failure 2 years ago after presenting with fatigue, purpura, dark-colored urine, and rapidly declining kidney functi
full:
A 46-year-old woman with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis developed kidney failure 2 years ago after presenting with fatigue, purpura, dark-colored urine, and rapidly declining kidney function. At that time, her serum creatinine increased from 0.9 mg/dL to 6.8 mg/dL over 4 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 82 to 7 mL/min/1.73 m2. Myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was positive and proteinase 3 ANCA testing was negative.
Urinalysis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 40 to 50 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimated proteinuria of 2.0 g/day. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis. Despite appropriate treatment, kidney function did not recover sufficiently, and she remained dependent on hemodialysis.
She subsequently achieved complete clinical remission. For the past 8 months, she has had no constitutional, skin, pulmonary, upper respiratory, neurologic, or other manifestations of active vasculitis. Her blood pressure is 132/78 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.8 C. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 0. She remains dialysis-dependent and is now being evaluated for kidney transplantation. Repeat testing continues to show myeloperoxidase ANCA positivity.
The transplant team is considering postponing transplantation solely because ANCA remains detectable. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach?
A. Delay transplantation for at least 12 months after ANCA becomes negative because persistent seropositivity predicts inevitable post-transplant recurrence
B. Delay transplantation until myeloperoxidase ANCA becomes negative even though complete clinical remission has been maintained for more than 6 months
C. Proceed with transplantation because she has maintained complete clinical remission for more than 6 months, and persistent ANCA positivity alone should not delay transplantation
D. Proceed with transplantation only if maintenance immunosuppression eliminates detectable ANCA before the transplant procedure
E. Avoid kidney transplantation because persistent ANCA positivity indicates ongoing active vasculitis despite the absence of clinical manifestations
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. Proceed with transplantation because she has maintained complete clinical remission for more than 6 months, and persistent ANCA positivity alone should not delay transplantation
PART C — Explanation
This patient developed kidney failure from ANCA-associated vasculitis and is now being evaluated for kidney transplantation. The key findings are that she has remained in complete clinical remission for 8 months and has no current manifestations of active vasculitis, although myeloperoxidase ANCA remains detectable.
According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.4.2.1, kidney transplantation should be delayed until a patient with ANCA-associated vasculitis has been in complete clinical remission for at least 6 months. Persistence of ANCA positivity should not by itself delay transplantation.

title: Q080 · The treating physician concludes that she has true refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis. Which of the following treatment modifications best reflects KDIGO guidance?
body: A 44-year-old woman was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis after presenting with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At diagnosis, her se
full:
A 44-year-old woman was diagnosed with myeloperoxidase ANCA-associated vasculitis after presenting with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At diagnosis, her serum creatinine had increased from 0.8 mg/dL to 3.1 mg/dL over 4 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 92 to 17 mL/min/1.73 m2. Myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was positive and proteinase 3 ANCA testing was negative. She began induction therapy with cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoids.
Urinalysis at diagnosis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 35 to 45 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimated proteinuria of 1.8 g/day.
A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed focal segmental necrotizing lesions and cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
Despite ongoing induction therapy, she has never achieved remission. She continues to have purpura and dark-colored urine, and her serum creatinine has increased further from 3.1 mg/dL to 3.8 mg/dL, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 17 to 13 mL/min/1.73 m2. Her blood pressure is 148/84 mmHg, heart rate is 86 beats per minute, and temperature is 36.9 C. Urinalysis continues to show 3+ blood and 2+ protein, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts, with proteinuria of 1.7 g/day.
Medication adherence has been confirmed, and evaluation has not identified infection, drug intolerance, malignancy, or another secondary driver of vasculitis. Because worsening kidney function could reflect either chronic damage or persistent activity, a repeat kidney biopsy is obtained and demonstrates ongoing active necrotizing and crescentic glomerular lesions.
The treating physician concludes that she has true refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis. Which of the following treatment modifications best reflects KDIGO guidance?
A. Add rituximab because cyclophosphamide was used for induction, with an increase in glucocorticoids as clinically appropriate
B. Continue the same cyclophosphamide regimen without modification because refractory disease should not prompt a change in induction therapy
C. Transition to azathioprine maintenance because persistent kidney abnormalities after induction establish that remission has been achieved
D. Reduce immunosuppression because progressive kidney failure during treatment should be assumed to represent irreversible chronic kidney damage
E. Discontinue induction therapy and observe because persistent ANCA-associated manifestations during treatment do not warrant additional immunosuppression
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Add rituximab because cyclophosphamide was used for induction, with an increase in glucocorticoids as clinically appropriate
PART C — Explanation
This patient has persistent systemic and kidney manifestations of ANCA-associated vasculitis despite cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoid induction and has never achieved remission. Potential explanations for apparent treatment resistance, including nonadherence, drug intolerance, infection, malignancy, and other secondary drivers, have been evaluated. In addition, repeat kidney biopsy demonstrates ongoing active disease rather than kidney dysfunction attributable solely to chronic damage. The presentation therefore supports true refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis.
According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.4.1.1, refractory disease can be treated by increasing glucocorticoids, either intravenously or orally, and by adding rituximab when cyclophosphamide induction has previously been used. Conversely, cyclophosphamide can be used when rituximab was the previous induction treatment. Plasma exchange can also be considered.

title: Q081 · The treating physician is considering adding plasma exchange solely because diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is present. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach?
body: A 39-year-old woman with proteinase 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis presents with a 4-day history of cough and recurrent blood-streaked sputum. She was diagnosed 2 weeks earlier after developing fatigue,
full:
A 39-year-old woman with proteinase 3 ANCA-associated vasculitis presents with a 4-day history of cough and recurrent blood-streaked sputum. She was diagnosed 2 weeks earlier after developing fatigue, nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and pulmonary manifestations. Proteinase 3 ANCA testing was positive and myeloperoxidase ANCA testing was negative. induction therapy with glucocorticoids and rituximab has already been started.
At presentation, her blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg, heart rate is 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.9 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. She does not require supplemental oxygen. Serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL compared with 0.9 mg/dL 3 weeks earlier, with estimated glomerular filtration rate changing from 82 to 75 mL/min/1.73 m2. Chest imaging demonstrates bilateral pulmonary infiltrates compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.
Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein, with 1 to 3 red blood cells per high-power field and no red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimates proteinuria of 0.2 g/day.
The treating physician is considering adding plasma exchange solely because diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is present. Which of the following best reflects the appropriate approach?
A. Continue appropriate induction therapy without automatically adding plasma exchange because the alveolar hemorrhage is not accompanied by hypoxemia
B. Add plasma exchange because any diffuse alveolar hemorrhage requires plasma exchange regardless of the patient’s oxygenation
C. Replace rituximab with plasma exchange because pulmonary hemorrhage should be treated with plasma exchange rather than immunosuppression
D. Change immediately to cyclophosphamide because diffuse alveolar hemorrhage requires cyclophosphamide whenever oxygen saturation remains normal
E. Withhold further immunosuppression because the absence of hypoxemia indicates that the pulmonary hemorrhage does not require treatment
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Continue appropriate induction therapy without automatically adding plasma exchange because the alveolar hemorrhage is not accompanied by hypoxemia
PART C — Explanation
This patient has diffuse alveolar hemorrhage associated with ANCA-associated vasculitis, but she remains well oxygenated with an oxygen saturation of 97% on room air and does not require supplemental oxygen. Her kidney function is also preserved, avoiding a separate kidney-related indication for considering plasma exchange.
According to KDIGO Practice Point 9.4.1.2, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with hypoxemia carries a high early mortality risk, and plasma exchange can be considered in addition to glucocorticoids with either cyclophosphamide or rituximab. In contrast, in the absence of hypoxemia, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage generally has a more favorable prognosis and responds as the extrapulmonary disease is controlled.

title: Q082 · The treating physician is choosing between a rituximab-based regimen and a daily cyclophosphamide-based regimen for remission induction and reviews the overall results of the RAVE trial. Which of the following best reflects the comparative efficacy demonstrated by that trial?
body: A 48-year-old man with no previous history of vasculitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, persistent nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His
full:
A 48-year-old man with no previous history of vasculitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, persistent nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 146/84 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Proteinase 3 ANCA testing is positive and myeloperoxidase ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine has increased from 0.9 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier to 2.4 mg/dL, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 88 to 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. There is no respiratory failure or requirement for assisted ventilation.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 25 to 35 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimates proteinuria of 1.6 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows focal segmental necrotizing lesions with cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating physician is choosing between a rituximab-based regimen and a daily cyclophosphamide-based regimen for remission induction and reviews the overall results of the RAVE trial. Which of the following best reflects the comparative efficacy demonstrated by that trial?
A. Rituximab was statistically superior to the cyclophosphamide-based regimen for the primary endpoint in the overall study population
B. Rituximab was noninferior to the cyclophosphamide-based regimen for achieving remission without prednisone at 6 months
C. Rituximab was inferior to the cyclophosphamide-based regimen and should be reserved for patients who cannot receive cyclophosphamide
D. Rituximab and cyclophosphamide achieved equivalent remission rates, but the trial was not designed to assess noninferiority
E. Rituximab demonstrated benefit only in relapsing disease and did not establish efficacy for newly diagnosed severe ANCA-associated vasculitis
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. Rituximab was noninferior to the cyclophosphamide-based regimen for achieving remission without prednisone at 6 months
PART C — Explanation
The RAVE trial was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy noninferiority trial comparing rituximab with daily cyclophosphamide for remission induction in severe, ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis. Rituximab was administered at 375 mg/m2 once weekly for 4 weeks, whereas the control group received daily cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day, with transition to azathioprine permitted after remission. Both groups received the same glucocorticoid regimen.
The primary endpoint was complete remission, defined by a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis of 0 together with successful discontinuation of prednisone at 6 months.
B is correct. The primary endpoint was reached by 63 of 99 patients receiving rituximab, or 64%, compared with 52 of 98 patients receiving the cyclophosphamide-based regimen, or 53%. This result satisfied the prespecified criterion for noninferiority, with P<0.001.

title: Q083 · The treating nephrologist considers either rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based remission induction but wonders whether one demonstrated a clearly better overall safety profile and reviews the RAVE trial before selecting therapy. Which of the following best reflects the safety findings of RAVE?
body: A 50-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3 ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with 6 weeks of fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and d
full:
A 50-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3 ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with 6 weeks of fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 144/82 mmHg, heart rate is 86 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.0 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Proteinase 3 ANCA testing is positive and myeloperoxidase ANCA testing is negative.
His serum creatinine has increased from 0.9 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier to 2.5 mg/dL, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 87 to 29 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 25 to 35 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. A spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio estimates proteinuria of 1.5 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows focal segmental necrotizing lesions with cellular crescents. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for immunoglobulins or complement. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist considers either rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based remission induction but wonders whether one demonstrated a clearly better overall safety profile and reviews the RAVE trial before selecting therapy. Which of the following best reflects the safety findings of RAVE?
A. The RAVE trial did not collect adverse-event data and therefore provided no comparative safety information
B. Rituximab demonstrated significantly fewer overall adverse events and therefore proved safer than cyclophosphamide-based therapy
C. Cyclophosphamide demonstrated significantly fewer overall adverse events and therefore had the better overall safety profile
D. Rituximab demonstrated fewer serious adverse events but more overall adverse events than the cyclophosphamide-based regimen
E. Rituximab did not demonstrate a significantly lower overall adverse-event rate than the cyclophosphamide-based regimen
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: E. Rituximab did not demonstrate a significantly lower overall adverse-event rate than the cyclophosphamide-based regimen
PART C — Explanation
The RAVE trial compared rituximab-based with cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy in severe ANCA-associated vasculitis. Although avoidance of cyclophosphamide toxicity was an important rationale for evaluating rituximab, the trial did not demonstrate a significant difference between the groups in total adverse events, serious adverse events, or non-disease-related adverse events.
E is correct because RAVE did not establish that rituximab had a significantly better overall adverse-event profile than the cyclophosphamide-based regimen. Therefore, the trial cannot be interpreted as proving that rituximab was safer overall.

title: Q084 · The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy but is concerned that rituximab may be less effective in the setting of major kidney involvement. The nephrologist reviews the renal subgroup findings from the RAVE trial. Which of the following best reflects the evidence from that subgroup?
body: A 56-year-old woman with no previous history of vasculitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 150/86 mm
full:
A 56-year-old woman with no previous history of vasculitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 150/86 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 9.
Serum creatinine is 3.2 mg/dL today. It was 0.9 mg/dL 6 weeks ago. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 74 mL/min/1.73 m2 6 weeks ago and is 16 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 35 to 45 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.8 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 18 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis in 6 glomeruli and cellular crescents in 7 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy but is concerned that rituximab may be less effective in the setting of major kidney involvement. The nephrologist reviews the renal subgroup findings from the RAVE trial. Which of the following best reflects the evidence from that subgroup?
A. Rituximab was superior to cyclophosphamide-based therapy, with primary-endpoint rates of 67% and 42%, respectively, P=0.01
B. Rituximab and cyclophosphamide-based therapy had similar efficacy, with primary-endpoint rates of 61% and 63%, respectively, P=0.92
C. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy was superior to rituximab, with primary-endpoint rates of 63% and 41%, respectively, P<0.01
D. Rituximab was inferior to cyclophosphamide-based therapy because kidney function improved only in the cyclophosphamide group
E. The comparative efficacy of rituximab and cyclophosphamide could not be assessed because patients with major renal disease were excluded from RAVE
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. Rituximab and cyclophosphamide-based therapy had similar efficacy, with primary-endpoint rates of 61% and 63%, respectively, P=0.92
PART C — Explanation
This patient has ANCA-associated vasculitis with major kidney involvement, demonstrated by rapidly worsening kidney function, red blood cell casts, and biopsy-confirmed necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis. These characteristics resemble the major renal disease subgroup evaluated in RAVE.
In RAVE, major renal disease was defined by the presence of at least one major renal Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis item, including urinary red blood cell casts, biopsy-confirmed glomerulonephritis, or an increase in serum creatinine of more than 30%.
B is correct. Among patients with major renal disease, 31 of 51 patients receiving rituximab, or 61%, reached the primary endpoint compared with 32 of 51 patients receiving the cyclophosphamide-based regimen, or 63%. The difference was not statistically significant, with P=0.92. Kidney function also improved in parallel during the first 6 months, with estimated creatinine clearance increasing by 11.2 mL/min in the rituximab group and 10.5 mL/min in the control group. The trial therefore did not demonstrate that rituximab was less effective than cyclophosphamide-based therapy in the major renal disease subgroup.

title: Q085 · The treating nephrologist is considering induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether its findings are applicable to this patient. Based on the characteristics of the population studied in RAVE, which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?
body: A 53-year-old man with no previous history of vasculitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, persistent nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His
full:
A 53-year-old man with no previous history of vasculitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, persistent nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 148/86 mmHg, heart rate is 86 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing is positive and MPO-ANCA testing is negative. His clinical findings are consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine is 2.7 mg/dL today. It was 0.9 mg/dL 6 weeks ago. The estimated glomerular filtration rate was 100 mL/min/1.73 m2 6 weeks ago and is 26 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.7 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 20 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 5 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 7 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether its findings are applicable to this patient. Based on the characteristics of the population studied in RAVE, which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?
A. This patient differs substantially from the RAVE population because patients with active kidney involvement and glomerulonephritis were excluded
B. This patient differs substantially from the RAVE population because only patients with relapsing microscopic polyangiitis and MPO-ANCA positivity were studied
C. This patient closely resembles the RAVE population because he has newly diagnosed, severe PR3-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis and a BVAS/WG above 3
D. This patient does not resemble the RAVE population because enrollment required a BVAS/WG of 0 before induction therapy
E. This patient does not resemble the RAVE population because only patients previously treated with cyclophosphamide were included
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. This patient closely resembles the RAVE population because he has newly diagnosed, severe PR3-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis and a BVAS/WG above 3
PART C — Explanation
This patient closely resembles the clinical population evaluated in RAVE. He has granulomatosis with polyangiitis, PR3-ANCA positivity, manifestations of severe active disease, and a BVAS/WG of 8. He is newly diagnosed, which was also represented in the study.
RAVE included patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis who had positive PR3-ANCA or MPO-ANCA testing, manifestations of severe disease, and a BVAS/WG of at least 3. Both newly diagnosed and relapsing disease were eligible.
C is correct because this patient satisfies each of those key disease characteristics. His presentation therefore resembles the population in whom rituximab and cyclophosphamide-based remission induction were evaluated. This means the RAVE evidence is reasonably applicable when his nephrologist considers the two treatment approaches; it does not mean that resemblance to the trial population alone mandates a particular treatment.

title: Q086 · The treating nephrologist reviews the cyclophosphamide-based comparator regimen used in the RAVE trial to determine how therapy was transitioned after remission. Which of the following most closely matches that treatment sequence?
body: A 58-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 15
full:
A 58-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 150/88 mmHg, heart rate is 84 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.0 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine is 2.9 mg/dL today. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks ago. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 72 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks ago and is 17 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.6 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 19 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 5 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 7 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
Cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy is selected along with glucocorticoids. Four months later, her systemic manifestations have resolved, her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0, serum creatinine has improved to 1.4 mg/dL, and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 43 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood and trace protein without red blood cell casts, and estimated proteinuria is 0.3 g/day.
The treating nephrologist reviews the cyclophosphamide-based comparator regimen used in the RAVE trial to determine how therapy was transitioned after remission. Which of the following most closely matches that treatment sequence?
A. Cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day until remission, followed by rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks as maintenance therapy
B. Cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day for 6 months regardless of remission, followed by azathioprine 1 mg/kg/day at month 6
C. Cyclophosphamide 1 mg/kg/day, adjusted for renal insufficiency, followed by azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day immediately after the first month
D. Cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day, adjusted for renal insufficiency, followed by azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day after remission between months 3 and 6
E. Cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day for 3 months, followed by mycophenolate mofetil after remission regardless of treatment response
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. Cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day, adjusted for renal insufficiency, followed by azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day after remission between months 3 and 6
PART C — Explanation
This patient has achieved remission 4 months after beginning cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy. The question asks how the cyclophosphamide comparator strategy used in RAVE transitioned once remission occurred.
In the RAVE control group, daily cyclophosphamide was administered at 2 mg/kg/day, with adjustment for renal insufficiency. Patients who achieved remission between months 3 and 6 were eligible to switch from cyclophosphamide to azathioprine at 2 mg/kg/day.
D is correct because it reproduces both components of the RAVE comparator strategy: cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day during induction, adjusted for renal insufficiency, followed by azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day when remission occurred between months 3 and 6. Because this patient achieved remission at month 4, her clinical course fits the timing of that transition.

His blood pressure is 146/84 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing is positive and MPO-ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine is 2.6 mg/dL today. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks ago. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 103 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks ago and is 29 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 25 to 35 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.5 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 21 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 5 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 6 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
Rituximab-based induction therapy is selected. Four months later, his systemic manifestations have resolved, his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0, serum creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL, and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 66 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood without red blood cell casts, estimated proteinuria is 0.3 g/day, and he has had no disease flares.
The treating nephrologist reviews the glucocorticoid regimen that accompanied both treatment strategies in the RAVE trial. Which of the following most closely reflects the glucocorticoid approach evaluated in that study?
A. One to three methylprednisolone pulses of 1000 mg each, followed by prednisone 1 mg/kg/day and tapering to discontinuation by month 5 if remission occurred without flares
B. One methylprednisolone pulse of 500 mg, followed by prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day and continuation of low-dose prednisone throughout the 6-month induction period
C. Three methylprednisolone pulses of 500 mg each, followed by prednisone 1 mg/kg/day and maintenance of prednisone 10 mg/day through month 6
D. One to three methylprednisolone pulses of 1000 mg each, followed by prednisone 1 mg/kg/day without tapering until completion of the 6-month induction period
E. Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day without intravenous methylprednisolone, followed by tapering only after completion of 6 months of induction therapy
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. One to three methylprednisolone pulses of 1000 mg each, followed by prednisone 1 mg/kg/day and tapering to discontinuation by month 5 if remission occurred without flares
PART C — Explanation
This patient is receiving rituximab-based induction therapy and has achieved remission without disease flares. The key point is that rituximab in RAVE was not evaluated without glucocorticoids. Both the rituximab and cyclophosphamide treatment groups received the same glucocorticoid regimen.
A is correct. In RAVE, both treatment groups received 1 to 3 pulses of methylprednisolone at 1000 mg each, followed by prednisone at 1 mg/kg/day. Prednisone was then tapered so that patients who achieved remission without disease flares had discontinued glucocorticoids by 5 months.
This accompanying treatment is important when interpreting the RAVE results. The trial compared rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based induction strategies while providing the same glucocorticoid regimen to both groups. Therefore, the remission outcomes cannot be interpreted as results of rituximab or cyclophosphamide given without glucocorticoid therapy.

He receives rituximab-based induction therapy with glucocorticoids. At the 6-month assessment, his constitutional, upper respiratory, skin, and kidney manifestations have resolved. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0. Serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 73 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood without red blood cell casts, and estimated proteinuria is 0.2 g/day. PR3-ANCA remains positive. He continues prednisone 5 mg/day because the prednisone taper has not yet been completed.
The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE trial to determine how this 6-month response corresponds to the study endpoints. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?
A. He does not meet the primary endpoint because the prednisone taper is incomplete despite a BVAS/WG of 0
B. He meets the primary endpoint because a BVAS/WG of 0 alone was sufficient to define the 6-month outcome
C. He meets the primary endpoint because prednisone below 10 mg/day satisfied the glucocorticoid component of that endpoint
D. He does not meet the primary endpoint because kidney function must return completely to the pretreatment baseline value
E. He does not meet the primary endpoint because persistent PR3-ANCA positivity excludes trial-defined remission
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. He does not meet the primary endpoint because the prednisone taper is incomplete despite a BVAS/WG of 0
PART C — Explanation
The RAVE primary endpoint required two components at 6 months: a BVAS/WG of 0 and successful completion of the prednisone taper. Both conditions had to be satisfied.
A is correct. This patient has no measurable active vasculitis at month 6, with a BVAS/WG of 0, but he remains on prednisone 5 mg/day. Because the prednisone taper has not been successfully completed, he does not meet the RAVE primary endpoint.
Importantly, his profile corresponds to a secondary endpoint evaluated in RAVE: BVAS/WG of 0 while receiving prednisone at a dose below 10 mg/day. Thus, prednisone 5 mg/day is compatible with that secondary remission endpoint but not with the primary endpoint requiring completion of the prednisone taper.

Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
She begins rituximab-based remission-induction therapy with glucocorticoids. At the 1-month assessment, serum creatinine has improved to 2.2 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 24 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis demonstrates 2+ blood and 1+ protein, with 15 to 20 red blood cells per high-power field and persistent red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.1 g/day. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis has decreased from 8 to 7. However, she has developed a new foot drop attributed to active vasculitic neuropathy.
The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE trial definitions to classify her response at 1 month. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?
A. She does not meet the definition of early treatment failure because BVAS/WG decreased by at least 1 point from baseline
B. She meets the definition of early treatment failure because a new disease manifestation developed despite a 1-point reduction in BVAS/WG
C. She does not meet the definition of early treatment failure because serum creatinine and estimated proteinuria have improved
D. She meets the definition of complete remission because kidney function improved and BVAS/WG decreased from baseline
E. She can be classified as a treatment success because early treatment failure required an increase in BVAS/WG at 1 month
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. She meets the definition of early treatment failure because a new disease manifestation developed despite a 1-point reduction in BVAS/WG
PART C — Explanation
RAVE defined early treatment failure at 1 month using either of two criteria: the BVAS/WG had not decreased by at least 1 point from baseline, or a new manifestation of disease had emerged. Patients meeting either criterion were counted as treatment failures for the primary endpoint.
B is correct. This patient’s BVAS/WG decreased from 8 to 7, satisfying the numerical requirement for at least a 1-point reduction. However, she developed a new vasculitic manifestation at the 1-month assessment. Because the RAVE definition used an “or” relationship, the new manifestation is sufficient to classify her as having early treatment failure despite the reduction in BVAS/WG.

The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE trial to determine how this 6-month response would correspond to its efficacy endpoints. Which of the following is the most accurate classification?
A. She meets the secondary remission endpoint but not the primary endpoint
B. She meets the primary endpoint but not the secondary remission endpoint
C. She meets both the primary and secondary remission endpoints
D. She meets neither the primary nor the secondary remission endpoint
E. She meets the definition of early treatment failure rather than remission
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. She meets the secondary remission endpoint but not the primary endpoint
PART C — Explanation
The distinction depends on the glucocorticoid component of the RAVE endpoints.
The primary RAVE endpoint required a BVAS/WG of 0 together with successful completion of the prednisone taper at 6 months. A separate secondary endpoint was a BVAS/WG of 0 while receiving prednisone at a dose below 10 mg/day.
A is correct. This patient has a BVAS/WG of 0 at 6 months and is taking prednisone 7.5 mg/day. Because 7.5 mg/day is below 10 mg/day, she satisfies the secondary remission endpoint. However, she has not completed the prednisone taper, so she does not satisfy the primary endpoint.

title: Q091 · The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE definitions to classify this change in disease activity. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?
body: A 51-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis initially presents with fatigue, nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Hi
full:
A 51-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis initially presents with fatigue, nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 148/86 mmHg, heart rate is 86 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.0 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing is positive and MPO-ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine is 2.6 mg/dL. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 86 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks earlier and is 28 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.6 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 19 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 5 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 6 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
He receives remission-induction therapy with glucocorticoids. At month 2, his systemic manifestations have resolved, his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0, serum creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate is 62 mL/min/1.73 m2, and estimated proteinuria is 0.3 g/day. At month 4, he develops recurrent palpable purpura over both lower limbs. Serum creatinine is 1.4 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 57 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated proteinuria remains 0.3 g/day. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis increases from 0 to 1.
The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE definitions to classify this change in disease activity. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation?
A. This does not meet the RAVE definition of disease flare because serum creatinine remained near its prior value
B. This does not meet the RAVE definition of disease flare because BVAS/WG must increase by at least 2 points
C. This meets the RAVE definition of disease flare because BVAS/WG increased by at least 1 point
D. This meets the RAVE definition of early treatment failure because any BVAS/WG increase before month 6 constitutes failure
E. This does not meet the RAVE definition of disease flare because kidney manifestations must recur together with extrarenal disease
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. This meets the RAVE definition of disease flare because BVAS/WG increased by at least 1 point
PART C — Explanation
In RAVE, a disease flare was defined as an increase in the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis of 1 point or more.
C is correct. At month 2, this patient had no measurable active vasculitic disease, with resolution of his systemic manifestations and a BVAS/WG of 0. At month 4, he develops recurrent palpable purpura, indicating renewed clinical disease activity. His BVAS/WG consequently increases from 0 to 1.
This is sufficient to meet the RAVE definition of a disease flare because the required threshold was an increase in BVAS/WG of at least 1 point. This patient has an increase of exactly 1 point, from 0 to 1, together with a recurrent vasculitic manifestation. Therefore, his presentation fulfills the trial-defined flare criterion.
The relatively stable kidney findings do not exclude a flare. His serum creatinine changes only from 1.3 mg/dL to 1.4 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate changes from 62 to 57 mL/min/1.73 m2, and estimated proteinuria remains 0.3 g/day. RAVE did not require deterioration in kidney function, recurrent red blood cell casts, or worsening proteinuria for a disease flare to be present. The defining criterion was an increase in BVAS/WG of at least 1 point. In this case, the recurrent purpura provides the new active vasculitic manifestation responsible for that increase.

Based on the trial’s noninferiority analysis, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion regarding induction therapy for this patient?

The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial before discussing the treatment options with the patient. Based on the trial’s noninferiority analysis, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion regarding induction therapy for this patient?
A. Rituximab is preferred because it demonstrated statistically superior overall induction efficacy compared with cyclophosphamide-based therapy
B. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy is preferred because rituximab demonstrated lower overall induction efficacy in the RAVE trial
C. Rituximab is an evidence-supported alternative because its overall induction efficacy was noninferior to cyclophosphamide-based therapy
D. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy remains the only evidence-supported option because noninferiority does not support use of rituximab for induction
E. Rituximab and cyclophosphamide-based therapy have identical efficacy because RAVE demonstrated exact equivalence between the two strategies
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. Rituximab is an evidence-supported alternative because its overall induction efficacy was noninferior to cyclophosphamide-based therapy
PART C — Explanation
This patient has newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis with active kidney involvement and requires induction therapy. His clinical presentation resembles the population evaluated in RAVE, which included patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis, PR3-ANCA or MPO-ANCA positivity, active severe disease, and both newly diagnosed and relapsing presentations.
C is correct. In the overall RAVE population, 64% of patients receiving rituximab reached the primary endpoint compared with 53% receiving cyclophosphamide-based therapy. The trial met its prespecified criterion for noninferiority. Therefore, for a patient such as this one, the RAVE evidence supports rituximab as an induction option without concluding that choosing rituximab means accepting substantially less effective therapy than the cyclophosphamide-based strategy.
The important clinical interpretation is that RAVE did not identify cyclophosphamide-based therapy as more effective overall. At the same time, it also did not prove that rituximab was superior in the overall study population. Although the numerical remission rate was higher with rituximab, the difference did not reach statistical significance for superiority. Thus, when the nephrologist is choosing between these two induction approaches for a patient resembling the RAVE population and without another trial-supported feature specifically favoring one strategy, the RAVE result supports rituximab as a noninferior alternative rather than establishing one regimen as universally better.
