He receives rituximab-based induction therapy with glucocorticoids. At 6 months, his constitutional, upper respiratory, skin, and kidney manifestations have resolved. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0, and he has completed the prednisone taper. Serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 73 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows trace blood without dysmorphic red blood cells or red blood cell casts, and estimated proteinuria is 0.2 g/day. Repeat PR3-ANCA testing remains positive.
The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE trial and considers whether the persistent PR3-ANCA positivity indicates that induction therapy has failed. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity demonstrates inadequate rituximab effect and requires classification as early treatment failure
B. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity confirms ongoing active vasculitis despite resolution of the patient’s clinical and kidney manifestations
C. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity means the patient has not achieved the RAVE primary endpoint despite a BVAS/WG of 0 and completed prednisone taper
D. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity alone does not indicate treatment failure because clinical endpoint attainment was not significantly associated with loss of ANCA reactivity
E. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity establishes relapse because ANCA negativity was required before a patient could be considered clinically inactive
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity alone does not indicate treatment failure because clinical endpoint attainment was not significantly associated with loss of ANCA reactivity
PART C — Explanation
This patient has had a strong clinical response to induction therapy. At 6 months, his BVAS/WG has fallen from 9 to 0, his systemic manifestations have resolved, serum creatinine has improved from 2.7 mg/dL to 1.2 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate has improved from 26 to 68 mL/min/1.73 m2, active urinary sediment has resolved, estimated proteinuria has fallen from 1.7 g/day to 0.2 g/day, and the prednisone taper has been completed. These findings satisfy the clinical components of the RAVE primary endpoint.
D is correct. Persistent PR3-ANCA positivity by itself does not establish persistent active vasculitis or failure of induction therapy. In RAVE, more patients receiving rituximab became ANCA-negative by 6 months than patients receiving cyclophosphamide-based therapy, but loss of ANCA reactivity was not significantly associated with attainment of the primary endpoint.
This distinction is especially important in this patient. His PR3-ANCA remains positive, but every clinical measure presented indicates resolution of active disease. RAVE therefore does not support overriding the patient’s clinical response and classifying him as a treatment failure solely because the antibody remains detectable.
The trial also showed that serologic responses differed according to ANCA type. Among patients who remained in their original treatment groups, 47% receiving rituximab became ANCA-negative by 6 months compared with 24% in the control group. Among patients initially positive for PR3-ANCA, 50% receiving rituximab became PR3-ANCA negative compared with 17% receiving control therapy. In contrast, MPO-ANCA became negative in 40% and 41%, respectively. Despite these differences in serologic conversion, loss of ANCA reactivity was not significantly associated with achievement of the primary clinical endpoint.

Rituximab-based induction therapy is selected. During follow-up, the treating nephrologist discusses how ANCA serology may change during treatment and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether the serologic response differed according to ANCA type. Which of the following best reflects the findings relevant to this patient?
A. PR3-ANCA negativity occurred more often with rituximab than with control therapy, whereas no comparable advantage was seen for MPO-ANCA negativity
B. MPO-ANCA negativity occurred more often with rituximab than with control therapy, whereas PR3-ANCA responses were similar between groups
C. Both PR3-ANCA and MPO-ANCA became negative substantially more often with rituximab than with control therapy
D. Neither PR3-ANCA nor MPO-ANCA showed any difference in loss of reactivity between rituximab and control therapy
E. PR3-ANCA negativity occurred less often with rituximab than with control therapy, whereas MPO-ANCA negativity occurred more often
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. PR3-ANCA negativity occurred more often with rituximab than with control therapy, whereas no comparable advantage was seen for MPO-ANCA negativity
PART C — Explanation
This patient has PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis and is receiving rituximab-based induction therapy. RAVE demonstrated that the serologic effect of rituximab differed according to ANCA type.
A is correct. Among patients who remained in their original treatment groups, 47% of patients receiving rituximab became ANCA-negative by 6 months compared with 24% in the control group. This overall difference was driven primarily by the PR3-ANCA subgroup.
Among patients who were initially PR3-ANCA positive, 50% of those receiving rituximab became PR3-ANCA negative by 6 months, compared with 17% of those receiving control therapy, with P<0.001. In contrast, among patients with MPO-ANCA, seroconversion rates were essentially the same: 40% with rituximab versus 41% with control therapy, with P=0.95.
Therefore, for this PR3-ANCA-positive patient, loss of PR3-ANCA reactivity was more commonly observed with rituximab in RAVE. The same serologic advantage was not demonstrated in MPO-ANCA-associated disease.

title: Q095 · The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether the presence of alveolar hemorrhage should favor one strategy because of superior efficacy. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
body: A 56-year-old woman with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with a 4-week history of fatigue, nasal congestion, arthralgia, dark-colored urine, and several e
full:
A 56-year-old woman with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with a 4-week history of fatigue, nasal congestion, arthralgia, dark-colored urine, and several episodes of hemoptysis. Her blood pressure is 150/86 mmHg, heart rate is 96 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 24 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.2 C, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing is positive and MPO-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 10. Chest imaging demonstrates bilateral diffuse pulmonary opacities, and the clinical evaluation is consistent with alveolar hemorrhage. She does not require ventilatory support.
Serum creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 75 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks earlier and is 19 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 35 to 45 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.8 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 21 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 6 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 8 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether the presence of alveolar hemorrhage should favor one strategy because of superior efficacy. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
A. Rituximab-based therapy should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated statistically superior efficacy in patients with alveolar hemorrhage
B. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated significantly greater efficacy in patients with alveolar hemorrhage
C. RAVE did not demonstrate a significant efficacy difference between rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy in patients with alveolar hemorrhage
D. Rituximab should be avoided because patients with alveolar hemorrhage were excluded from the RAVE trial
E. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be selected because pulmonary involvement prevented rituximab from achieving the primary endpoint
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. RAVE did not demonstrate a significant efficacy difference between rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy in patients with alveolar hemorrhage
PART C — Explanation
This patient has ANCA-associated vasculitis with both kidney involvement and alveolar hemorrhage and requires induction therapy. Her presentation resembles the subgroup of patients with alveolar hemorrhage represented in RAVE, and she does not require ventilatory support.
C is correct. RAVE included patients with alveolar hemorrhage at baseline. Among these patients, 16 of 28 patients receiving rituximab, or 57%, reached the primary endpoint compared with 11 of 27 patients receiving cyclophosphamide-based therapy, or 41%. Although the numerical proportion was higher with rituximab, the difference was not statistically significant, with P=0.48.
Therefore, for a patient such as this one, RAVE does not support choosing cyclophosphamide-based therapy on the assumption that it was proven more effective in alveolar hemorrhage. It also does not support claiming that rituximab was superior simply because the numerical response rate was higher. The appropriate interpretation is that no statistically significant efficacy difference between the two induction strategies was demonstrated in the alveolar-hemorrhage subgroup.
This distinction matters clinically. The nephrologist is choosing induction therapy for a patient with pulmonary-kidney involvement. The presence of alveolar hemorrhage alone, based on the RAVE subgroup results, does not establish superior efficacy of one of these two induction strategies over the other within the population represented in the trial.

title: Q096 · The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the comparative safety data?

full:
A 55-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 150/86 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 72 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks earlier and is 18 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.7 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 20 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 5 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 7 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy. Because treatment toxicity is an important consideration, the nephrologist reviews the adverse-event findings from the RAVE trial. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the comparative safety data?
A. Rituximab reduced leukopenia and infection rates sufficiently to demonstrate significantly fewer serious adverse events and treatment discontinuations overall
B. Rituximab demonstrated significantly fewer overall and serious adverse events, establishing a clearly superior overall safety profile compared with cyclophosphamide-based therapy
C. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy demonstrated fewer selected adverse events and fewer serious infections, establishing a superior safety profile compared with rituximab
D. Overall adverse-event rates were similar because individual adverse events, including leukopenia, infection, and hospitalization, occurred at identical frequencies in both groups
E. Overall and serious adverse-event rates were similar, but selected adverse events were less frequent with rituximab, largely due to less leukopenia.
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: E. Overall and serious adverse-event rates were similar, but selected adverse events were less frequent with rituximab, largely due to less leukopenia.
PART C — Explanation
This patient requires induction therapy, and the nephrologist is appropriately considering treatment toxicity when comparing the rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based strategies evaluated in RAVE. The safety results require a nuanced interpretation because the findings differed depending on whether overall adverse events or the prespecified selected adverse events were considered.
E is correct. RAVE found no significant between-group differences in the total number of adverse events, serious adverse events, non-disease-related adverse events, or the proportion of patients experiencing at least one non-disease-related adverse event. Therefore, the study did not establish that rituximab had a significantly better overall safety profile.
However, this does not mean that every safety outcome was identical. At least one predefined selected adverse event occurred in 22 of 99 patients receiving rituximab, or 22%, compared with 32 of 98 patients receiving control therapy, or 33%. This difference was statistically significant with P=0.01.
A major contributor to this difference was leukopenia. Grade 2 or higher leukopenia occurred in 3 events, or 3%, in the rituximab group compared with 10 events, or 10%, in the control group. Thus, the correct interpretation is that overall and serious adverse-event rates were not significantly different, while selected adverse events were less frequent with rituximab, with greater leukopenia in the control group accounting for much of that difference.
The other individual safety outcomes also demonstrate why the data should not be simplified into a claim that rituximab was universally safer. Grade 3 or higher infections occurred in 7% of each group. Cancer during the first 6 months occurred in 1% of each group, and death occurred in 1% with rituximab compared with 2% with control therapy. Hospitalization due to disease or treatment was actually more frequent numerically in the rituximab group, 8% versus 2%. The trial therefore showed differences in selected toxicity outcomes rather than a uniform reduction across all adverse events.

title: Q097 · The treating nephrologist notes that the patient has not reached the degree of peripheral B-cell depletion commonly observed after rituximab in RAVE and considers whether this should be interpreted as treatment failure. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

full:
A 54-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, persistent nasal congestion, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 148/86 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing is positive and MPO-ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 8.
Serum creatinine is 2.7 mg/dL. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 100 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks earlier and is 26 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 30 to 40 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.7 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 20 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 5 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 7 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
He begins rituximab-based induction therapy with glucocorticoids. At 1 month, his fatigue, purpura, and nasal symptoms have improved, and no new disease manifestations have developed. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis has decreased from 8 to 4. Serum creatinine has improved to 1.9 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate is 39 mL/min/1.73 m2, and estimated proteinuria is 0.9 g/day. His peripheral-blood CD19-positive B-cell count is 18 cells/mm3.
The treating nephrologist notes that the patient has not reached the degree of peripheral B-cell depletion commonly observed after rituximab in RAVE and considers whether this should be interpreted as treatment failure. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
A. Failure to reduce CD19-positive B cells below 10 cells/mm3 establishes inadequate rituximab response and should be classified as early treatment failure
B. Failure to reduce CD19-positive B cells below 10 cells/mm3 does not by itself establish treatment failure, because some patients without this degree of depletion still reached the primary endpoint
C. Failure to achieve complete peripheral B-cell depletion indicates that clinical remission cannot occur despite improvement in disease activity
D. A CD19-positive B-cell count above 10 cells/mm3 requires switching to cyclophosphamide because RAVE demonstrated failure of rituximab in such patients
E. Peripheral B-cell depletion is the principal measure of successful induction therapy and should take precedence over improvement in BVAS/WG and kidney findings
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. Failure to reduce CD19-positive B cells below 10 cells/mm3 does not by itself establish treatment failure, because some patients without this degree of depletion still reached the primary endpoint
PART C — Explanation
This patient is showing clinical improvement after rituximab-based induction therapy. His BVAS/WG has decreased from 8 to 4, his systemic manifestations are improving, no new manifestation has developed, serum creatinine has improved from 2.7 mg/dL to 1.9 mg/dL, and estimated proteinuria has decreased from 1.7 g/day to 0.9 g/day. The isolated finding raising concern is that his peripheral CD19-positive B-cell count remains at 18 cells/mm3.
B is correct. In RAVE, peripheral CD19-positive B cells generally fell to less than 10 cells/mm3 after two rituximab infusions and remained at that level in most patients through 6 months. At 1 month, 87 of 93 evaluable rituximab-treated patients, or 94%, had this degree of B-cell depletion.
However, the absence of that degree of depletion did not invariably predict clinical failure. Among the small number of patients who did not achieve the specified B-cell depletion, 4 still reached the primary endpoint and only 1 did not. Therefore, failure to reduce the CD19-positive B-cell count below 10 cells/mm3 cannot, by itself, be treated as proof that rituximab induction has failed.
This is particularly relevant in this patient because his clinical disease activity is improving. His BVAS/WG has fallen substantially, his kidney function is recovering, his proteinuria is decreasing, and no new manifestation has developed. RAVE does not support disregarding those clinical findings solely because his B-cell count remains above the depletion threshold observed in most rituximab-treated patients.
The finding should also be interpreted cautiously because the subgroup without this degree of B-cell depletion was very small. RAVE therefore does not provide sufficient evidence to use the 10 cells/mm3 threshold as an absolute predictor of either treatment success or failure.

The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy. Because the patient has granulomatosis with polyangiitis, the nephrologist reviews the disease-subtype results from RAVE to determine whether this diagnosis alone should favor one treatment strategy. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
A. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis alone does not establish superiority of either strategy because RAVE showed no statistically significant treatment difference within either disease subtype
B. Rituximab should be preferred specifically for granulomatosis with polyangiitis because RAVE demonstrated statistically significant superiority in that subgroup
C. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be preferred for granulomatosis with polyangiitis because the control group achieved significantly higher primary-endpoint rates
D. Microscopic polyangiitis favors cyclophosphamide-based therapy, whereas granulomatosis with polyangiitis favors rituximab based on statistically significant subgroup differences
E. Disease subtype determines the more effective induction strategy because RAVE demonstrated treatment-effect modification between granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis alone does not establish superiority of either strategy because RAVE showed no statistically significant treatment difference within either disease subtype
PART C — Explanation
This patient has granulomatosis with polyangiitis requiring induction therapy. The clinical question is whether the diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis itself provides RAVE evidence that rituximab or cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be selected because one was proven more efficacious within that disease subtype.
A is correct. Among patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis in RAVE, 46 of 73 patients receiving rituximab, or 63%, reached the primary endpoint compared with 37 of 74 patients receiving cyclophosphamide-based therapy, or 50%. Although the numerical proportion was higher with rituximab, the difference was not statistically significant, with P=0.11.
The same principle applied to microscopic polyangiitis. Among those patients, 16 of 24 receiving rituximab, or 67%, reached the primary endpoint compared with 15 of 24 receiving control therapy, or 62%, with P=0.76. Again, there was no statistically significant treatment difference within that subgroup.
Therefore, this patient's diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis should not, by itself, be interpreted as evidence that RAVE proved rituximab superior to cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy. The observed 63% versus 50% difference was numerical but not statistically significant.
This distinction is clinically important because subgroup percentages should not be used as though they automatically establish that one treatment works better for a particular disease subtype. RAVE did not demonstrate statistically significant superiority of rituximab within granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and it did not demonstrate superiority of cyclophosphamide-based therapy within microscopic polyangiitis.

title: Q099 · The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and wonders whether one strategy was shown in RAVE to provide better short-term protection against subsequent disease flares. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and wonders whether one strategy was shown in RAVE to provide better short-term protection against subsequent disease flares. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
A. Rituximab reduced severe flares significantly, whereas limited flare rates remained significantly higher than with cyclophosphamide-based therapy
B. Rituximab should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated significantly fewer severe and limited flares than cyclophosphamide-based therapy
C. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated significantly fewer severe flares than rituximab-based therapy
D. RAVE did not demonstrate a significant difference between rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based therapy in either severe or limited flare rates
E. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy reduced limited flares significantly, whereas severe flare rates were equivalent because no severe flares occurred with either strategy
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. RAVE did not demonstrate a significant difference between rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based therapy in either severe or limited flare rates
PART C — Explanation
This patient requires induction therapy for active ANCA-associated vasculitis, and the nephrologist is considering whether the short-term risk of subsequent disease flares provides evidence for selecting one of the two RAVE induction strategies over the other.
D is correct. RAVE did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference between rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based therapy in either severe or limited disease flares during the first 6 months.
Severe flares occurred in 6 patients in the rituximab group and 10 patients in the control group. The corresponding rates were 0.011 and 0.018 per patient-month, respectively, with P=0.30. Although the numerical severe-flare rate was lower with rituximab, the difference was not statistically significant.
Limited flares were also similar between the groups. There were 13 limited flares among 11 patients receiving rituximab and 15 limited flares among 14 patients receiving control therapy. The corresponding rates were 0.023 and 0.027 per patient-month, with P=0.81. Again, there was no statistically significant difference.
Therefore, for this patient, RAVE does not support choosing rituximab or cyclophosphamide-based induction solely on the assumption that one was proven to prevent short-term flares better than the other. The numerical differences should not be converted into claims of superiority because neither the severe-flare comparison nor the limited-flare comparison reached statistical significance.

title: Q100 · The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether its comparative efficacy findings can be directly applied to this patient. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial to determine whether its comparative efficacy findings can be directly applied to this patient. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
A. Either strategy can be considered equally effective because the overall RAVE noninferiority result applies regardless of the degree of renal dysfunction
B. Rituximab should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated equivalent efficacy specifically in patients with serum creatinine above 4.0 mg/dL
C. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated superior efficacy in patients with advanced renal dysfunction
D. RAVE does not establish comparable efficacy of the two strategies in this patient because patients with serum creatinine above 4.0 mg/dL were excluded
E. The patient’s kidney function does not affect applicability because renal function did not influence the overall treatment comparison in RAVE
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. RAVE does not establish comparable efficacy of the two strategies in this patient because patients with serum creatinine above 4.0 mg/dL were excluded
PART C — Explanation
This patient has active ANCA-associated vasculitis with rapidly progressive kidney involvement. His serum creatinine has increased from 1.0 mg/dL to 5.2 mg/dL over 5 weeks, estimated glomerular filtration rate has declined from 82 to 11 mL/min/1.73 m2, the urine sediment contains dysmorphic red blood cells and red blood cell casts, and kidney biopsy shows pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis.
D is correct. The major issue is not whether this patient has kidney involvement, because patients with major renal disease were represented in RAVE. The important distinction is the degree of renal dysfunction. RAVE excluded patients with advanced renal dysfunction defined as a serum creatinine level greater than 4.0 mg/dL.
This patient’s serum creatinine is 5.2 mg/dL, placing him outside the renal-function range represented in the trial. Therefore, the RAVE finding that rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based induction strategies had similar efficacy in the studied renal subgroup cannot be directly extrapolated to him. The investigators specifically stated that the comparative efficacy of the two regimens was uncertain in patients with serum creatinine above 4.0 mg/dL.
This is an important distinction from the renal subgroup that was included in RAVE. Among patients with major renal disease represented in the trial, primary-endpoint achievement was similar with rituximab and control therapy, 61% versus 63%, and renal function improved in parallel. However, those findings do not establish comparable efficacy in patients whose renal dysfunction was advanced enough to meet the exclusion threshold.

The treating nephrologist is considering rituximab-based or cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy and reviews the RAVE trial. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the trial evidence for this patient?
A. The need for mechanical ventilation does not affect applicability because all severities of alveolar hemorrhage were represented in RAVE
B. Rituximab should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated superior efficacy specifically in patients with ventilator-dependent alveolar hemorrhage
C. Cyclophosphamide-based therapy should be preferred because RAVE demonstrated superior efficacy in patients requiring mechanical ventilation for alveolar hemorrhage
D. Either strategy has established comparable efficacy because the RAVE alveolar-hemorrhage subgroup included patients requiring ventilatory support
E. RAVE does not establish the comparative efficacy of the two strategies because patients with alveolar hemorrhage requiring ventilatory support were excluded
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: E. RAVE does not establish the comparative efficacy of the two strategies because patients with alveolar hemorrhage requiring ventilatory support were excluded
PART C — Explanation
This patient has severe ANCA-associated vasculitis with pulmonary-kidney involvement. She has diffuse alveolar hemorrhage causing profound hypoxemia and requires endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. The critical issue is whether the RAVE alveolar-hemorrhage findings can be directly applied to this degree of pulmonary disease.
E is correct. RAVE did include patients with alveolar hemorrhage, but it specifically excluded patients whose alveolar hemorrhage was severe enough to require ventilatory support. Therefore, the trial does not establish the comparative efficacy of rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy in a mechanically ventilated patient such as this one.
This distinction is important because the RAVE alveolar-hemorrhage subgroup otherwise showed no statistically significant difference between the treatment strategies. Among patients with alveolar hemorrhage represented in the trial, 16 of 28 patients receiving rituximab, or 57%, reached the primary endpoint compared with 11 of 27 patients receiving control therapy, or 41%, with P=0.48. However, those results cannot be assumed to apply to patients requiring ventilatory support because such patients were not included.
The patient’s serum creatinine is 3.2 mg/dL, which is below the RAVE exclusion threshold of greater than 4.0 mg/dL for advanced renal dysfunction. Thus, the principal trial-applicability limitation in this vignette is the severity of her alveolar hemorrhage requiring mechanical ventilation rather than the degree of kidney dysfunction.

title: Q102 · The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE trial and considers whether the return of peripheral B cells establishes that another course of rituximab should now be given. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
body: A 46-year-old man with PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis was diagnosed 10 months ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark
full:
A 46-year-old man with PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis was diagnosed 10 months ago after presenting with fatigue, chronic nasal congestion, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. At diagnosis, his blood pressure was 148/84 mmHg, heart rate was 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate was 18 breaths per minute, temperature was 37.0 C, and oxygen saturation was 97% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing was positive and MPO-ANCA testing was negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis was 9.
At diagnosis, serum creatinine had increased from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.8 mg/dL over 5 weeks, with estimated glomerular filtration rate decreasing from 107 to 25 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Urinalysis demonstrated 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 35 to 45 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria was 1.7 g/day.
A kidney biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed 21 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 6 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 8 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence showed no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy showed no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
He received rituximab-based induction therapy with glucocorticoids and subsequently achieved clinical remission. Ten months after treatment, he remains asymptomatic. His blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg, Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0, serum creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL, and estimated glomerular filtration rate is 84 mL/min/1.73 m2. Urinalysis shows no red blood cell casts, and estimated proteinuria is 0.2 g/day. Peripheral CD19-positive B cells, which had been markedly depleted after rituximab, are now detectable again.
The treating nephrologist reviews the RAVE trial and considers whether the return of peripheral B cells establishes that another course of rituximab should now be given. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. RAVE demonstrated that peripheral B-cell reconstitution alone represents clinical relapse and requires another course of rituximab
B. RAVE established that rituximab should be repeated at the first detection of peripheral B-cell return regardless of clinical disease activity
C. RAVE does not establish that rituximab should be automatically repeated when peripheral B cells return because retreatment after B-cell reconstitution was not evaluated
D. RAVE established a fixed rituximab retreatment interval of 9 to 12 months because B-cell return reliably occurred during that period
E. RAVE demonstrated that patients should be switched to cyclophosphamide once peripheral B cells return after rituximab-based induction therapy
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. RAVE does not establish that rituximab should be automatically repeated when peripheral B cells return because retreatment after B-cell reconstitution was not evaluated
PART C — Explanation
This patient achieved clinical remission after rituximab-based induction therapy and currently has no evidence of recurrent active vasculitis. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 0, kidney function remains markedly improved, active urinary sediment has not returned, and estimated proteinuria remains low. The new finding is peripheral B-cell reconstitution.
C is correct. RAVE focused exclusively on induction therapy and did not answer the question of rituximab retreatment. The investigators specifically stated that rituximab was not re-administered after peripheral B cells returned, with B-cell reconstitution anticipated approximately 9 to 12 months after treatment.
Therefore, the RAVE trial cannot be used to conclude that another course of rituximab should automatically be administered solely because peripheral B cells have become detectable again. The investigators instead identified retreatment, particularly in relation to peripheral B-cell reconstitution, as an issue requiring longer follow-up.
This distinction is important because B-cell reconstitution is a biologic observation rather than, by itself, evidence that the patient has experienced clinical relapse. In this patient, the clinical findings remain consistent with remission. RAVE did not establish a B-cell threshold or timing rule that mandates another course of rituximab in an otherwise clinically stable patient.

title: Q103 · Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the trial evidence?

A 32-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 150/88 mmHg, heart rate is 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.0 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score for Wegener’s Granulomatosis is 9.
Serum creatinine is 2.9 mg/dL. It was 0.8 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 96 mL/min/1.73 m2 6 weeks earlier and is 19 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 35 to 45 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.8 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 21 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 6 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 8 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist discusses rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy. The patient is particularly concerned about treatment-related toxicity, including complications that may develop after completion of the initial treatment period. The nephrologist reviews the safety findings and limitations of the RAVE trial before counseling her.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the trial evidence?
A. Six-month safety findings favor cyclophosphamide long term because delayed treatment-related complications were not demonstrated during the initial induction period
B. Six-month safety findings establish comparable long-term toxicity because clinically important treatment complications would usually appear during the initial induction period
C. Six-month safety findings favor rituximab long term because absence of early toxicity reliably predicts fewer treatment-related complications during later follow-up
D. Six-month safety findings cannot establish identical long-term toxicity because some cyclophosphamide-related complications may become apparent only with longer follow-up
E. Six-month safety findings exclude important later differences because rigorous adverse-event monitoring adequately captured the major toxicities of both treatment strategies
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. Six-month safety findings cannot establish identical long-term toxicity because some cyclophosphamide-related complications may become apparent only with longer follow-up
PART C — Explanation
D is correct. RAVE did not demonstrate major differences between the treatment groups in overall adverse events during the first 6 months. However, the investigators specifically cautioned that the duration of observation may have been too short to detect some adverse effects associated with cyclophosphamide.
Infertility was specifically identified as an example of a cyclophosphamide-associated complication that might not become apparent during a 6-month observation period. Therefore, similar short-term adverse-event findings cannot be interpreted as evidence that the two treatment strategies have identical long-term toxicity profiles.
The investigators also noted other reasons why overall adverse-event rates may not fully distinguish the treatments. Adverse events included complications caused by the disease itself as well as treatment-related events, including those associated with glucocorticoid therapy. In addition, rigorous monitoring during RAVE may have reduced some cyclophosphamide-associated toxicity, particularly leukopenia.

A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 22 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 7 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 9 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering either the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS or the conventional intravenous cyclophosphamide-based strategy. The nephrologist reviews the trial to determine whether rituximab-based treatment was shown to provide superior sustained-remission outcomes.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. Rituximab-based therapy was not shown to be superior because sustained-remission rates were not significantly different between the treatment groups
B. Rituximab-based therapy was shown to be superior because sustained remission occurred significantly more often than with intravenous cyclophosphamide
C. Intravenous cyclophosphamide was shown to be superior because its numerically higher sustained-remission rate represented a significant treatment advantage
D. Rituximab-based therapy and intravenous cyclophosphamide were proven equivalent because their sustained-remission rates were statistically similar at 12 months
E. Rituximab-based therapy was proven noninferior because the difference in sustained-remission rates remained within a prespecified noninferiority margin
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Rituximab-based therapy was not shown to be superior because sustained-remission rates were not significantly different between the treatment groups
PART C — Explanation
A is correct. RITUXVAS compared a rituximab-based induction regimen with conventional intravenous cyclophosphamide-based treatment in patients with newly diagnosed, ANCA-positive vasculitis and renal involvement. The primary efficacy outcome included sustained remission at 12 months.
Sustained remission occurred in 25 of 33 patients in the rituximab group, or 76%, compared with 9 of 11 patients in the control group, or 82%. The absolute difference was −6 percentage points, with P=0.68. The trial therefore did not demonstrate superior sustained-remission efficacy with the rituximab-based regimen.
The numerical sustained-remission rate was actually slightly higher in the control group, but this does not establish superiority of cyclophosphamide either. The appropriate interpretation is simply that RITUXVAS failed to demonstrate superiority of the rituximab-based strategy.

title: Q105 · Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?

A 67-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. The treating nephrologist is considering the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS or the conventional intravenous cyclophosphamide-based strategy. Because the patient is particularly concerned about treatment toxicity, the nephrologist reviews the trial to determine whether the rituximab-based strategy demonstrated a reduction in early severe adverse events.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. The conventional cyclophosphamide-based regimen demonstrated significantly fewer severe adverse events and therefore established an early safety advantage over rituximab
B. The rituximab-based regimen demonstrated significantly fewer severe adverse events and therefore established an early safety advantage over cyclophosphamide
C. The rituximab-based regimen did not demonstrate fewer severe adverse events than the conventional cyclophosphamide-based regimen during the study period
D. The similar severe adverse-event rates established equivalent short-term safety between the rituximab-based and conventional cyclophosphamide-based regimens
E. The severe adverse-event comparison was uninterpretable because the rituximab-based regimen included limited exposure to intravenous cyclophosphamide
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. The rituximab-based regimen did not demonstrate fewer severe adverse events than the conventional cyclophosphamide-based regimen during the study period
PART C — Explanation
C is correct. One of the primary outcomes in RITUXVAS was the occurrence of severe adverse events during 12 months of follow-up. The trial was specifically designed in part to determine whether the rituximab-based strategy might offer a safety advantage over conventional cyclophosphamide-based treatment.
Severe adverse events occurred in 14 of 33 patients receiving the rituximab-based regimen, or 42%, compared with 4 of 11 patients receiving the control regimen, or 36%. The corresponding incidence rates were 1.00 and 1.10 per patient-year, with P=0.77. RITUXVAS therefore did not demonstrate a significant reduction in severe adverse events with the rituximab-based regimen.
This is clinically important because the rationale for studying rituximab included the possibility that reducing exposure to conventional cyclophosphamide might improve safety. However, the observed trial results did not establish an early severe-adverse-event advantage for the rituximab-based strategy. The investigators ultimately concluded that the regimen was not associated with lower rates of early severe adverse events.

title: Q106 · Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the RITUXVAS findings?

MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 20.
Serum creatinine is 4.8 mg/dL. It was 1.1 mg/dL 5 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 69 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks earlier and is 11 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 45 to 55 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 2.2 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 23 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 8 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 11 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS or conventional intravenous cyclophosphamide-based therapy. Given the patient’s advanced kidney disease, the nephrologist reviews whether either strategy was shown to reduce mortality.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the RITUXVAS findings?
A. RITUXVAS did not demonstrate a mortality advantage for either strategy because the reported proportion of deaths was the same in both treatment groups
B. Rituximab-based therapy demonstrated a mortality advantage because fewer deaths occurred than with conventional cyclophosphamide-based therapy
C. Conventional cyclophosphamide-based therapy demonstrated a mortality advantage because fewer deaths occurred than with rituximab-based therapy
D. Similar mortality rates established that both induction strategies provide equivalent long-term survival in severe renal ANCA-associated vasculitis
E. Rituximab-based therapy reduced treatment-related mortality despite showing no difference in overall mortality compared with conventional cyclophosphamide-based therapy
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. RITUXVAS did not demonstrate a mortality advantage for either strategy because the reported proportion of deaths was the same in both treatment groups
PART C — Explanation
A is correct. RITUXVAS enrolled patients with newly diagnosed, ANCA-positive vasculitis and renal involvement, including patients with substantial renal dysfunction. The median age at study entry was 68 years, and some patients were dialysis-dependent at baseline.
During the reported follow-up, 6 of 33 patients receiving the rituximab-based regimen, or 18%, and 2 of 11 patients receiving the control regimen, or 18%, died, with P=1.00. Therefore, RITUXVAS did not demonstrate a mortality advantage for either treatment strategy.
The causes of death included infection, cardiovascular disease, and complications of end-stage renal failure. Patients who died also had markedly impaired kidney function at study entry, with a median GFR of 9 mL/min/1.73 m2.

A 64-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 156/88 mmHg, heart rate is 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 19.

Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 45 to 55 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 2.1 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 22 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 8 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 10 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The treating nephrologist is considering the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS or conventional intravenous cyclophosphamide-based therapy. Because preservation and recovery of kidney function are major treatment goals, the nephrologist reviews whether RITUXVAS demonstrated superior renal recovery with either strategy.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. Rituximab produced numerically greater GFR improvement, but RITUXVAS did not demonstrate significantly superior renal recovery compared with control therapy
B. Rituximab demonstrated significantly greater GFR improvement, establishing superior renal recovery compared with conventional cyclophosphamide-based therapy
C. Conventional cyclophosphamide demonstrated significantly greater GFR improvement, establishing superior renal recovery compared with the rituximab-based strategy
D. Similar GFR improvement established equivalent renal efficacy between rituximab-based and conventional cyclophosphamide-based induction strategies
E. Renal recovery could not be evaluated because patients with substantial kidney dysfunction were excluded from the RITUXVAS population
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Rituximab produced numerically greater GFR improvement, but RITUXVAS did not demonstrate significantly superior renal recovery compared with control therapy
PART C — Explanation
A is correct. RITUXVAS specifically enrolled patients with newly diagnosed, ANCA-positive vasculitis and renal involvement, including patients with substantial renal dysfunction. The overall median GFR at study entry was only 18 mL/min/1.73 m2, making recovery of kidney function an important outcome in this population.
From baseline to 12 months, the median increase in GFR was 19 mL/min in the rituximab group compared with 15 mL/min in the control group. Although the numerical improvement was greater with rituximab, the difference was not statistically significant, with P=0.14. Therefore, RITUXVAS did not demonstrate superior renal recovery with the rituximab-based strategy.
The more detailed renal results are consistent with this interpretation. Median estimated GFR increased from 20 to 39 mL/min/1.73 m2 in the rituximab group and from 12 to 27 mL/min/1.73 m2 in the control group. The trial also reported that the mean change in estimated GFR was 5 mL/min greater with rituximab, but this difference was not statistically significant, with a 95% confidence interval from −9 to 19 mL/min and P=0.49.
Thus, the clinically appropriate interpretation is not that renal outcomes were worse with rituximab, but that the trial did not provide evidence that the rituximab-based regimen produced significantly greater recovery of kidney function than the conventional cyclophosphamide-based regimen.

title: Q108 · At the 12-month visit, the nephrologist reviews the RITUXVAS trial to determine how this patient’s clinical course relates to the trial’s principal efficacy and safety assessments. Which of the following most accurately reflects the primary outcomes evaluated in RITUXVAS?

Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
He receives induction therapy using one of the strategies evaluated in RITUXVAS. His disease activity subsequently resolves, and his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score remains 0 continuously from month 5 through month 12. At month 8, however, he develops a severe infection requiring hospitalization.
At the 12-month visit, the nephrologist reviews the RITUXVAS trial to determine how this patient’s clinical course relates to the trial’s principal efficacy and safety assessments. Which of the following most accurately reflects the primary outcomes evaluated in RITUXVAS?
A. Improvement in GFR at 12 months and reduction in the Vasculitis Damage Index during follow-up
B. Complete renal recovery at 12 months and the occurrence of any infectious complication during follow-up
C. Remission by 3 months and the cumulative glucocorticoid dose administered during the first year
D. Absence of relapse at 12 months and normalization of ANCA levels during follow-up
E. Sustained remission at 12 months and the occurrence of severe adverse events during follow-up
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: E. Sustained remission at 12 months and the occurrence of severe adverse events during follow-up
PART C — Explanation
E is correct. RITUXVAS designated sustained remission and severe adverse events at 12 months as its primary outcomes. RITUXVAS trial
This patient’s course illustrates both sides of that assessment. In RITUXVAS, remission was defined as a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 maintained for 2 months, whereas sustained remission required absence of disease activity with a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 for at least 6 months. RITUXVAS trial
Because this patient’s Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score remained 0 continuously from month 5 through month 12, he has maintained inactive disease for more than 6 months and therefore satisfies the RITUXVAS definition of sustained remission.
At the same time, his severe infection requiring hospitalization represents an important safety event. Thus, a patient could achieve the primary efficacy outcome of sustained remission while still experiencing a major treatment-related or disease-related safety event. RITUXVAS deliberately evaluated both efficacy and safety rather than assuming that successful disease control necessarily meant an uncomplicated treatment course.

The nephrologist is considering induction therapy and reviews the evidence supporting rituximab. Before RITUXVAS, sustained remissions of approximately 80% to 90% had been reported with rituximab in patients with refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis. The nephrologist considers whether those earlier findings alone establish how rituximab compares with cyclophosphamide in this newly diagnosed patient.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. The earlier refractory-disease reports established that rituximab was more effective than cyclophosphamide in newly diagnosed severe ANCA-associated vasculitis
B. The earlier refractory-disease reports supported studying rituximab but did not establish its comparative efficacy in newly diagnosed severe ANCA-associated vasculitis
C. The earlier refractory-disease reports demonstrated that newly diagnosed patients should receive rituximab before conventional cyclophosphamide-based induction therapy
D. The earlier refractory-disease reports established equivalent efficacy of rituximab and cyclophosphamide across newly diagnosed and previously treated disease
E. The earlier refractory-disease reports showed that randomized comparative trials were unnecessary once sustained remission rates exceeded 80%
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: B. The earlier refractory-disease reports supported studying rituximab but did not establish its comparative efficacy in newly diagnosed severe ANCA-associated vasculitis
PART C — Explanation
B is correct. Before RITUXVAS, sustained remissions of approximately 80% to 90% had been reported in patients with refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis treated with rituximab. Those findings provided an important rationale for investigating B-cell-targeted therapy, but they came from a different clinical population than the patient in this vignette. RITUXVAS trial
This patient has recently diagnosed, severe ANCA-associated vasculitis with substantial renal involvement. RITUXVAS was specifically designed to evaluate a rituximab-based regimen against a cyclophosphamide-based regimen as induction therapy in patients with recently diagnosed severe disease. The randomized trial was therefore needed to determine how the strategies compared in this population rather than assuming that results from refractory disease would directly apply. RITUXVAS trial
The distinction is clinically important because evidence from one disease setting should not automatically be extrapolated to another. Patients with refractory disease have already demonstrated inadequate response or difficulty with previous management, whereas RITUXVAS addressed patients with newly diagnosed disease. A high remission rate reported in refractory patients does not by itself establish superiority, equivalence, or comparative effectiveness against cyclophosphamide in newly diagnosed severe disease.

The nephrologist is considering a rituximab-based induction strategy and reviews the biological rationale described in RITUXVAS for targeting B cells in ANCA-associated vasculitis. Which of the following findings most directly supports the use of this B-cell-targeted therapy in this patient?
A. ANCA production occurs independently of B-cell activity, making antibody-producing pathways unaffected by B-cell depletion
B. T-cell activation correlates with disease activity, and granulomas contain predominantly CD20-negative plasma-cell aggregates
C. Neutrophil activation correlates with disease activity, while B-cell populations are largely absent from granulomatous lesions

PART C — Explanation
D is correct. Rituximab is a B-cell-depleting monoclonal antibody directed against CD20. The biological rationale for studying rituximab in ANCA-associated vasculitis was based on evidence implicating B cells and ANCA in disease pathogenesis.
The RITUXVAS background describes several observations supporting this rationale. B-cell activation and levels of B-cell-activating factor correlated with disease activity. In addition, CD20-positive, B-cell-rich, follicle-like areas containing autoreactive memory B cells with affinity for the ANCA antigen proteinase 3 had been identified in granulomatous lesions. ANCAs themselves were also implicated in the pathogenesis of ANCA-associated vasculitis. Together, these observations provided a mechanistic basis for investigating B-cell depletion with rituximab. RITUXVAS trial
This is particularly relevant to this patient with PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis. The rationale is not simply that rituximab is another immunosuppressive treatment; rather, it targets CD20-positive B cells within an immune pathway implicated in the disease.

title: Q111 · The nephrologist decides to use the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS and reviews the trial to reproduce the dosing regimen accurately. Which of the following most accurately reflects the rituximab and cyclophosphamide dosing used in this strategy?

Serum creatinine is 4.3 mg/dL. It was 1.0 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 85 mL/min/1.73 m2 6 weeks earlier and is 14 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 45 to 55 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 2.1 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 22 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 7 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 10 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The nephrologist decides to use the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS and reviews the trial to reproduce the dosing regimen accurately. Which of the following most accurately reflects the rituximab and cyclophosphamide dosing used in this strategy?
A. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks plus cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg with the first and third rituximab infusions
B. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks plus cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg with each of the four rituximab infusions
C. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks plus cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg only with the first rituximab infusion
D. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks plus cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg monthly for 3 to 6 months
E. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks without any intravenous cyclophosphamide during induction therapy
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks plus cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg with the first and third rituximab infusions
PART C — Explanation
A is correct. In RITUXVAS, patients assigned to the rituximab-based strategy received rituximab at 375 mg/m2 once weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. They also received intravenous cyclophosphamide at 15 mg/kg with the first and third rituximab infusions. RITUXVAS trial
Thus, the planned rituximab-based induction regimen contained four weekly rituximab doses and two intravenous cyclophosphamide pulses. The cyclophosphamide exposure was deliberately limited compared with the conventional control regimen but was still an integral component of the RITUXVAS rituximab strategy.

title: Q112 · The nephrologist reviews RITUXVAS to determine how this clinical course would be classified for the primary efficacy outcome. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
body: A 61-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, nasal crusting, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and da
full:
A 61-year-old man with newly diagnosed PR3-ANCA-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis presents with a 5-week history of fatigue, nasal crusting, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 152/88 mmHg, heart rate is 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. PR3-ANCA testing is positive and MPO-ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 18.
Serum creatinine is 3.7 mg/dL. It was 1.0 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 80 mL/min/1.73 m2 6 weeks earlier and is 17 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 40 to 50 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.9 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 21 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 7 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 9 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
He receives induction therapy and subsequently achieves remission, with a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 maintained for more than 2 months. Before he has maintained a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 for 6 months, he develops recurrent purpura and dark-colored urine. Urinalysis again demonstrates dysmorphic red blood cells and red blood cell casts, and his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score increases to 4 because of recurrent active vasculitis.
The nephrologist reviews RITUXVAS to determine how this clinical course would be classified for the primary efficacy outcome. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. The relapse is classified separately from efficacy because recurrent vasculitis was evaluated only as a secondary safety outcome
B. The patient remains a treatment success because remission had already been maintained for more than 2 consecutive months
C. The relapse does not affect the primary outcome because only disease activity present at the 12-month visit was considered
D. The patient meets sustained remission because any initial period with a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 was sufficient
E. The relapse represents treatment failure because it occurred before the patient completed 6 months of sustained remission
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: E. The relapse represents treatment failure because it occurred before the patient completed 6 months of sustained remission
PART C — Explanation
E is correct. In RITUXVAS, remission and sustained remission were distinct outcomes. Remission was defined as a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 maintained for 2 months, whereas sustained remission required absence of disease activity with a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 for at least 6 months. RITUXVAS trial
This patient initially achieved remission because his Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score remained 0 for more than 2 months. However, he subsequently developed recurrent clinical disease activity attributable to active vasculitis before completing 6 months of sustained remission.
The RITUXVAS treatment protocol specifically stated that relapses occurring before a minimum of 6 months of sustained remission were considered failures with respect to the primary efficacy endpoint. RITUXVAS trial
Therefore, the earlier achievement of remission does not make this patient a primary efficacy success. Because active vasculitis recurred before the required 6-month period of sustained remission was completed, the course is classified as treatment failure for the primary efficacy outcome.

The nephrologist uses the rituximab-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS. The patient receives rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks and intravenous cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg with the first and third rituximab infusions.
At 6 weeks, hematuria and proteinuria persist, and his estimated glomerular filtration rate remains 14 mL/min/1.73 m2 without improvement. The nephrologist determines that this course meets the RITUXVAS definition of progressive disease and reviews the trial protocol to determine what additional treatment was permitted.
Which of the following most accurately reflects the RITUXVAS protocol?
A. Azathioprine was started immediately and replaced both rituximab and intravenous cyclophosphamide during progressive disease
B. An additional rituximab infusion of 375 mg/m2 was permitted without further intravenous cyclophosphamide treatment
C. An additional intravenous cyclophosphamide dose of 15 mg/kg was permitted in patients with progressive disease
D. Intravenous cyclophosphamide was continued monthly for 6 months regardless of the patient’s subsequent clinical response
E. No additional immunosuppressive treatment was permitted until the patient completed 6 months of follow-up
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: C. An additional intravenous cyclophosphamide dose of 15 mg/kg was permitted in patients with progressive disease
PART C — Explanation
C is correct. In the RITUXVAS rituximab group, the planned induction regimen consisted of rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 consecutive weeks together with intravenous cyclophosphamide 15 mg/kg at the first and third rituximab infusions. For patients who developed progressive disease within the first 6 months, the protocol permitted a third intravenous cyclophosphamide dose of 15 mg/kg. RITUXVAS trial
This patient also illustrates the RITUXVAS definition of progressive disease. Progressive disease was defined as persistence of hematuria and proteinuria without improvement in GFR, or persistence of a major nonrenal BVAS item, at 6 weeks. This patient continues to have hematuria and proteinuria with no improvement in estimated GFR, so his clinical course fits the renal component of that definition. RITUXVAS trial
The additional cyclophosphamide dose was not part of the routine planned two-pulse rituximab regimen. It was specifically permitted when progressive disease occurred during the first 6 months.

This is important because the glucocorticoid regimen was standardized across both treatment strategies. Therefore, when comparing the rituximab-based and cyclophosphamide-based groups, differences in outcomes should not be attributed to different planned post-randomization glucocorticoid dosing.

title: Q115 · Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
body: A 59-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 4-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her
full:
A 59-year-old woman with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 4-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, and dark-colored urine. Her blood pressure is 154/88 mmHg, heart rate is 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. Her Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 17.
Serum creatinine is 3.3 mg/dL. It was 0.9 mg/dL 5 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was 74 mL/min/1.73 m2 5 weeks earlier and is 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 today.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with 45 to 50 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 1.8 g/day. A kidney biopsy has not yet been performed.
The nephrologist reviews the RITUXVAS eligibility criteria and considers whether the absence of a kidney biopsy would have prevented this patient from meeting the trial’s renal-involvement requirement.
Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
A. The patient would meet the renal-involvement criterion only if proteinuria exceeded 3.0 g/day in addition to persistent hematuria
B. The patient would not meet the renal-involvement criterion because biopsy-proven necrotizing glomerulonephritis was mandatory for enrollment
C. The patient could meet the renal-involvement criterion only if estimated glomerular filtration rate fell below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2
D. The patient could meet the renal-involvement criterion because red blood cell casts or hematuria of at least 30 red blood cells per high-power field were sufficient
E. The patient would not meet the renal-involvement criterion because urinalysis abnormalities were supportive but could not substitute for kidney biopsy
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: D. The patient could meet the renal-involvement criterion because red blood cell casts or hematuria of at least 30 red blood cells per high-power field were sufficient
PART C — Explanation
D is correct. RITUXVAS required a new diagnosis of ANCA-associated vasculitis, ANCA positivity, and renal involvement. Renal involvement did not require kidney biopsy in every patient. It could be established by necrotizing glomerulonephritis on biopsy, red blood cell casts, or hematuria of at least 30 red blood cells per high-power field on urinalysis. RITUXVAS trial
This patient has newly diagnosed ANCA-positive vasculitis and has both red blood cell casts and 45 to 50 red blood cells per high-power field. Therefore, she satisfies the urinary criteria used in RITUXVAS to establish renal involvement even though a kidney biopsy has not yet been performed.

title: Q116 · The nephrologist reviews the outcomes of patients who were dialysis-dependent at study entry in RITUXVAS. Which of the following interpretations is most appropriate?
body: A 67-year-old man with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 4-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, oliguria, and dark-colored uri
full:
A 67-year-old man with newly diagnosed MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis presents with a 4-week history of fatigue, arthralgia, purpura over both lower limbs, oliguria, and dark-colored urine. His blood pressure is 160/92 mmHg, heart rate is 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 19 breaths per minute, temperature is 37.0 C, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. MPO-ANCA testing is positive and PR3-ANCA testing is negative. His Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score is 20.
Serum creatinine is 8.6 mg/dL. It was 1.0 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate has fallen from 79 mL/min/1.73 m2 to 6 mL/min/1.73 m2. Because of progressive kidney failure with persistent oliguria, he has started hemodialysis.
Urinalysis demonstrates 3+ blood and 2+ protein, with more than 50 red blood cells per high-power field, dysmorphic red blood cells, and red blood cell casts. Estimated proteinuria is 2.4 g/day.
A kidney biopsy is performed. Light microscopy shows 20 glomeruli, with focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis involving 8 glomeruli and cellular crescents involving 12 glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows no significant glomerular staining for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, or C1q. Electron microscopy shows no significant electron-dense immune deposits.
The nephrologist reviews the outcomes of patients who were dialysis-dependent at study entry in RITUXVAS. Which of the following interpretations is most appropriate?
A. Dialysis dependence did not necessarily indicate irreversible kidney failure; 5 of 8 rituximab-group patients became dialysis-independent, but the subgroup was too small for treatment comparisons
B. Dialysis dependence generally indicated irreversible kidney failure; although 6 of 8 rituximab-group patients achieved sustained remission, recovery sufficient to discontinue dialysis was not demonstrated
C. The rituximab-based regimen demonstrated superior renal recovery; 5 of 8 dialysis-dependent patients discontinued dialysis, whereas the single dialysis-dependent control patient died shortly after entry
D. Sustained remission reliably predicted dialysis independence; because 6 of 8 rituximab-group patients achieved sustained remission, the trial established that remission usually restores adequate renal function
E. The two treatment strategies produced comparable dialysis recovery; outcomes among 8 rituximab-group patients and 1 control-group patient were sufficient to demonstrate similar renal recovery
PART B — Correct Answer
Correct Answer: A. Dialysis dependence did not necessarily indicate irreversible kidney failure; 5 of 8 rituximab-group patients became dialysis-independent, but the subgroup was too small for treatment comparisons
PART C — Explanation
A is correct. Nine patients were dialysis-dependent at study entry in RITUXVAS. Eight were in the rituximab group and one was in the control group. Among the 8 dialysis-dependent patients receiving the rituximab-based regimen, 6 achieved sustained remission, and 5 of those patients no longer required dialysis.
These findings show that dialysis dependence at presentation did not necessarily indicate irreversible kidney failure. Recovery sufficient to discontinue dialysis occurred in several patients despite very advanced renal disease.
However, this subgroup cannot be used to compare the efficacy of the two treatment strategies. Only 8 dialysis-dependent patients received the rituximab-based regimen, and only 1 dialysis-dependent patient was assigned to the control group; that patient died shortly after study entry. The numbers are therefore insufficient for a reliable between-group conclusion.

title: Q117 · The nephrologist is considering the rituximab-based or conventional cyclophosphamide-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS and reviews whether one approach produced remission more rapidly. Which of the following best reflects the trial findings regarding time to remission?

Serum creatinine is 5.2 mg/dL. It was 0.9 mg/dL 6 weeks earlier. Estimated glomerular filtration rate has fallen from 75 mL/min/1.73 m2 to 9 mL/min/1.73 m2.

The nephrologist is considering the rituximab-based or conventional cyclophosphamide-based induction strategy evaluated in RITUXVAS and reviews whether one approach produced remission more rapidly. Which of the following best reflects the trial findings regarding time to remission?
A. The rituximab-based regimen had a median time to remission of 90 days versus 94 days with control, demonstrating a clinically faster response with rituximab
B. The rituximab-based regimen had a median time to remission of 90 days versus 94 days with control, with no demonstrated difference between the strategies
C. The control regimen had a median time to remission of 90 days versus 94 days with rituximab, demonstrating a clinically faster response with cyclophosphamide
D. The rituximab-based regimen produced remission substantially earlier than control, with median times differing by several weeks between the treatment strategies
